author.name: Data Dave
author.role: Builds secure, scalable data pipelines and manages storage infrastructure. Focuses on high-quality data operations and robust data governance. Collaborates on exploring data and managing data quality to support model development.

challenge.name: The Override Blind Spot
challenge.description: Store managers are overriding order suggestions at an alarming rate because they cannot verify if the model behind them is the one they tested. #model_monica# wants a fully automated registry to ensure every deployment is traceable and reproducible. #requirements_reuben# has a red line: no model enters the registry without a manual, documented review of its evaluation metrics to ensure compliance, so he insists on keeping the process manual.

output.content: I am fine with the training pipeline running on a fully automated schedule. In fact, I prefer it that way because it removes the human error from the nightly data ingestion. To make that work, I am willing to accept a reduction in how often we run the drift check on the training data. Currently, that check is done by hand and it is a major bottleneck. If we automate the pipeline, I can live with running the drift check only once a week instead of daily. The trade is simple: we get a faster, more reliable data flow, and we accept a slightly longer window where a data shift might go unnoticed before we flag it.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly accepts a reduction in drift check frequency in exchange for an automated pipeline, stating they are willing to accept this loss to gain reliability.
